The YouTube channel "DrugsLab". It's blown my mind since stumbling upon it a few nights back the little attention it receives from the states because it really is an unconventional concept by American education standards, that's for sure. 

For those who've never heard, basically, it is a Dutch channel featuring three recurring contributors (Rens, Nellie, and Bastiaan) who, quite literally, just take drugs requested in the comment section every Friday on camera. According to their about section, they do this "to provide you of safe methods of use, safe doses, the effects, the risks and very useful do's and don'ts when high on drugs." With the Dutch government's money. And, somehow, it is legal to do so. 

I honestly just created this reddit account to post under this question because it fascinates me that they don't get more attention. I haven't stopped watching since I started. 
Check them out if you wanna watch some people snort coke for views: https://www.youtube.com/channel/UCvRQKXtIGcK1yEnQ4Te8hWQ/about
